blind_spots.blind_spot: UbiVision's 'full identity graph' tracks individuals across cameras, time, and spaces for commercial security use cases
blind_spots.operator_reality: Applied to an Army JPEO A&A Battlefield Automation deployment, continuous cross-camera personnel tracking is exactly the kind of PII/biometric data flow that triggers RMF/ATO review and CMMC data-handling controls — the site never addresses classification, access control, or data retention for that graph on a government network.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product materials are written for commercial buyers (retail, manufacturing, municipalities) where identity tracking is a feature, not a compliance liability.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Full identity graph — Track individuals across cameras, time, and spaces — not just faces.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The 'edge-first, cloud optional, works offline' architecture is marketed purely as a customer-choice privacy feature, not a DDIL requirement
blind_spots.operator_reality: For a battlefield-automation deployment this isn't optional — it's the whole game (intermittent tactical network, no fixed workstation, multi-node relay). The materials never describe what happens when the 'workstation' tier itself is mobile or the link between edge and workstation drops.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Framing throughout is 'your data never leaves the premises' — a privacy/compliance pitch aimed at retail and manufacturing customers with a fixed facility, not a contested or mobile tactical environment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Edge → Workstation → Cloud — Flexible deployment; works offline; the customer controls the data path.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Founder's original DoD-funded work was GPS-denied navigation for austere/lunar conditions, but flagship messaging has drifted to soft commercial verticals
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Defense' now sits as one line in a 6-item vertical list alongside hospitality and childcare security — suggests the org's center of gravity, hiring, and roadmap prioritization may not be built around hardening Ubivision-C for actual battlefield conditions, risking the same fielding gap that kills the fresh Army Phase II contract at transition.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The pivot narrative is explicit in their own timeline ('Pivoted to commercial spatial intelligence platform', 2023) even though a new Army Phase II award followed in 2024.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 12+ verticals, config only — Manufacturing, retail, transit, defense, community, hospitality — one backbone, configured per industry.

opener_hook: The $1.9M JPEO A&A Battlefield Automation award funds Ubivision-C — does the identity-graph pipeline hold up over a DDIL tactical link the way it does across the 400+ municipal camera network?
what_they_do: Edge AI computer-vision platform (UbiVision) turning existing camera networks into real-time spatial intelligence for security and operations, sold mainly to commercial verticals with defense as one of several use cases.
